logline: A New York couple inherit a crumbling mansion only to discover it is haunted by ghosts from different historical eras - and that the wife alone can see and speak to them after a near-death accident.

renewal.note: CBS renewed Ghosts for a sixth season in February 2025. Season 5 concluded in May 2026. Season 6 is in production.

bollymeter.basis: Rotten Tomatoes Season 1 at 87% from 15 critics; Metacritic logged 69; Decider called the characters funny with potential for fun storylines right off the bat.

pull_quotes.text: Ghosts is not only funny, but its characters show potential for fun storylines right off the bat.

seasons.review_body: The US adaptation of the BBC's Ghosts launched on CBS in October 2021 and quickly became a rare network comedy success story. Developers Joe Port and Joe Wiseman transplanted the British format to a Hudson Valley mansion, populating it with American historical ghosts - a Revolutionary War soldier, a 1990s finance bro, a Lenape tribesman, a Jazz Age singer. Rose McIver and Utkarsh Ambudkar anchored the living-couple dynamic with warmth that avoided the format's obvious sentimentality traps. Critics at 87 percent on Rotten Tomatoes praised the ensemble's range. Decider highlighted the characters' storyline potential. The Pittsburgh Tribune-Review noted well-drawn archetypes and broad but often quite funny comedy. Season 1's 18-episode order allowed the ghost ensemble to develop individual comic identities before the format had fully settled.

episode_reviews.title: Pilot
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Samantha and Jay inherit Woodstone Mansion and discover it is haunted after Samantha's near-death accident grants her the ability to see ghosts. The premiere introduces the full ensemble and establishes the show's core comic engine: the gulf between ghost-world logic and living-world practicality.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Samantha's first conversation with the full ghost ensemble - each demanding her attention for utterly different reasons - establishes the show's ensemble comedy rhythm.

critic_note.text: Ghosts is not only funny, but its characters show potential for fun storylines right off the bat.

bollymeter.basis: Rotten Tomatoes Season 2 achieved 100% - a perfect critical consensus - confirming the show had found its footing and exceeded the first season's critical reception.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 of Ghosts earned a perfect 100 percent on Rotten Tomatoes - a critical leap from the already-solid first season. The ensemble had fully settled into their ghost archetypes, and the writers had found the tonal range between silly setpiece comedy and genuinely affecting character-level storytelling. With 22 episodes, the season built out individual ghost backstories and relationships while maintaining the Samantha-Jay anchor. The CBS platform gave the show network-scale viewership that streaming comedies rarely reach: it ranked as one of the most-watched CBS comedies in years. Critics who had cautiously approved the premise in Season 1 now called the execution consistently impressive.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 is where Ghosts fully earns its premise - the ensemble dynamics that Season 1 promised arrive with consistency, and the 100% Rotten Tomatoes score reflects a comedy that has found its rhythm.

bollymeter.basis: Metacritic Season 3 at 81; Paste Magazine noted the show can still make viewers think and grow despite its comfortable familiarity - a sign of genuine craft in a network comedy.

pull_quotes.text: A program as comfortable and familiar as this one can continue to make us think and grow.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 aired on a reduced 10-episode order in early 2024 as part of CBS's mid-season schedule. Metacritic rated it at 81 - the show's best individual Metacritic score. Paste Magazine's observation that a comfortable, familiar show can still prompt thought and growth identified what Ghosts does better than most network comedies: it uses its genre constraints productively rather than hiding within them. The shorter run gave individual ghost storylines more focus than the sprawling second season managed. The CBS format and its broad network audience coexist with genuinely smart comedy writing - a combination the show's consistent critical appreciation reflects.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 3's compressed 10-episode order delivers the show's most focused run, letting individual ghost characters breathe without the pacing diffusion that longer network seasons risk.

bollymeter.basis: Collider noted Season 4 is on its way back to exploring new emotional landscapes; the show returned to its full 22-episode CBS order with critical consensus holding steady.

pull_quotes.text: The Port and Wiseman sitcom is on its way back to exploring new, emotional landscapes.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 returned in October 2024 with a full 22-episode CBS order. Collider identified the season as exploring new emotional landscapes after Season 3's more contained run. At this stage of the show's run, Ghosts operates as a reliable network comedy with strong character development infrastructure - the ghost ensemble has become one of the more genuinely differentiated ensembles in broadcast comedy. The show's February 2025 renewal for both Season 5 and 6 signalled CBS's confidence in a comedy that had outlasted most of its contemporaries.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 4 reopens the full episode count and broadens the ghost ensemble's emotional range after Season 3's focused sprint.

seasons.review_body: Season 5 premiered October 16, 2025 and concluded May 21, 2026. Critical aggregates were not available at the time of this filing. The show's sixth season renewal in early 2025 confirmed CBS's long-term commitment to one of its most reliably reviewed comedies.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 5 extends the show's CBS run with critical data still accumulating at filing time.
